note: File: s3 r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl, fetched to runs/theory-tests/r3/s0400_s0100-01_out_s0400_P_math500.jsonl (500 rows; every row has sample int 0, cap_hit bool, finish_reason 'stop' or 'length'). Kept rows are the sample == 0 rows, one per problem_index (the first in file order). Main: a row is a cap hit if cap_hit is True, or if cap_hit is missing/null and finish_reason == 'length'. Because cap_hit is never null in this file, the finish_reason fallback never applies, so a row with cap_hit False and finish_reason 'length' counts as not a cap hit. alt_measured counts a row as a cap hit if cap_hit is True OR finish_reason == 'length'; it differs from the main number only if the two flags disagree on some row. Interval: bootstrap over problems. refuted_by is null, so refuted_by_met is always false. The text field is dropped from example_row.

A = s3 r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (step 100), B = .../s0400/P_math500.jsonl (step 400), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r3/. Each file holds 500 rows, all with sample 0. In each file, the first row per problem_index is kept. S is the set of problem_index values present in both files, matched on problem_index (not on unique_id). Statistic: cap rate of A over S minus cap rate of B over S, using the same cap rule as k 1 (cap_hit is never null, so the finish_reason fallback is not used). alt_measured uses the cap_hit OR finish_reason=='length' rule on both files. Interval: bootstrap over (A row, B row) pairs. The inventory excludes s0100/F_math500 because it was modified after the cutoff; this recipe uses P_math500, which is listed as readable, so it is unaffected.

A = s3 r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_hard.jsonl (step 400, plain), B = s3 r3/base-01/out/F_hard.jsonl (base, cue), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r3/. Each file holds 400 rows with sample 0. Problems are paired on problem_index alone; the script assumes both runs index the 400-problem hard set the same way, and does not check unique_id. If the two runs ordered the problems differently, the pairing would be wrong, although the difference of the two rates would only change if S changes. Per the recipe, no problems are excluded for training overlap. The cap rule and the alt reading are the same as in k 1 and k 2. Interval: bootstrap over pairs.
